proposal.rule: d10/d12 (stage_5_segmentation): block boundaries mis-registered against visible joints at 15 px tolerance while ring count and prompt row are correct implies the template geometry priors (K_height, segment_width) rather than detection or denoising; r_fix_template: set block heights/widths to the geometry actually measured on this scan. Stage-1 is locked (residual 2.8 cm < 10 cm gate) so unfolding is untouched; denoising/enhancing are left alone because depth_nan_ratio (0.13) and retained ratio (0.77) are healthy and the worked examples show that broad joint perturbations of those stages collapsed sam_fill_rate (0.67 -> 0.30-0.43).
proposal.failure_mode: f_template_mismatch (with downstream f_crop_offset): K_height/segment_width priors not matching the K height (~845 mm) and ring pitch (~1216 mm) measured from the detected joint lines, shifting B1/B2/A crops and their SAM boundaries relative to the true joints.
proposal.rationale: In stage 5 the K crop half-height is 0.5*K_height and the B1/B2 crop centres sit at K_centre -/+ (0.5*K_height + 0.5*AB_height), so an error of ~30 mm in K_height moves every A/B boundary by ~3 px and a 150 mm error by ~15 px, which is exactly the correspondence_f1@15 tolerance; segment_width sets the crop half-width, and a width below the 1216 mm pitch leaves uncovered columns between rings while a width above it lets neighbouring rings overwrite each other. Both are read directly from the incumbent detected_lines.png (green/red K chains 169 px apart; vertical pitch 243.1 px), so the overlay pins the SAM template to the scan geometry instead of a generic prior. This is a minimal two-parameter stage-5 change: it cannot alter ring_count_error or depth_nan_ratio (upstream of SAM), and it is expected to raise correspondence_f1@15 by aligning block boundaries with the visible K/AB joints and to hold or raise sam_fill_rate through gap-free ring coverage. Values are inside bounds (K_height 700-1000, segment_width 1000-1400) and unfolding, denoising, enhancing and detecting keys are deliberately untouched.
